name: Morrow & Sons Salvage Boot
description: One of the few actual brands operating out of the Shelf, Morrow & Sons assembles boots from decommissioned industrial footwear — pulling good uppers off damaged soles and vice versa, mixing and matching until something serviceable emerges. The result is a boot that's visibly composite: different textures on each side, a toe box from one model, a shaft from another. They're tagged with a small hand-stamped 'M&S' near the ankle.
functionality: Sturdy construction. No special features, but built to outlast most new budget boots.
what_it_says: You buy local. You trust craft over corporate. There's a quiet pride in a Morrow pair.
story_hooks: Morrow & Sons keeps a ledger of every boot sold. If you can get to it, you can find out who was walking around when.
A pair of M&S boots on a Tier 3 body is a story — either they fell hard, or they never forgot where they came from.
